title: Group Anagrams
summary: Put words in the same group whenever their letters can be rearranged into one another.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–10,000 strings. Each has 0–100 lowercase English letters.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare the multiset of groups after sorting the words in each group. Keep multiplicities.

statement: Put words in the same group whenever their letters can be rearranged into one another. Return the groups as a list of lists. Keep every input occurrence, including copies of the same word. Both group order and order inside a group are free.

examples.explanation: The three words built from a, e and t form one group. The two words built from n, s and u form the other.
Both empty strings belong together. The other two have different counts of b.
All three share a signature, and both copies of mood remain.

constraints: 1–10,000 strings. Each has 0–100 lowercase English letters.
hints: Conceptual: Anagrams share a fingerprint based on how often each letter occurs.
Directional: Make a hashable signature using the 26 letter counts.
Implementation: Use each signature as a map key and append the original word to that key's list.
complexityAnalysis: O(L + 26n) expected time and O(26g) auxiliary space excluding returned groups. L counts input letters, n counts words, and g counts distinct signatures.
